idea-plugin.name: insrc
idea-plugin.description:
insrc brings the insrc code-knowledge system into the JetBrains IDE family — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm — from a single install. It is a thin orchestrator that owns no reasoning of its own: it wires insrc's grounded-analyze and tracked-workflow capabilities into the IDE's own AI assistant and manages the backing daemon, so your assistant answers from a citation-grounded model of your codebase rather than guessing.

What is insrc?

insrc is a local-first code-knowledge daemon. It parses your repos with tree-sitter into a typed entity/relation graph (backed by LMDB) and a vector store (LanceDB) for semantic search, then serves two things to your AI assistant over a private MCP server:

  • Grounded analyze — every answer about your code is built from real graph queries and embedded search, and each claim is cited to a specific file and symbol. No raw file dumps, no hallucinated paths — the assistant reasons over a verified, dependency-scoped model of the codebase.
  • A tracked workflow — a human-in-the-loop authoring pipeline that takes one request from triage → design → review → plan → build → code-review, producing an approved, cited artifact at every stage and refusing to advance until you approve the one before it. Every change, large or small, is tracked; a defect fix routes through a first-class bugfix path that captures reproduction and root cause and can open, link, and close a GitHub issue for you.

All of this runs on your machine and reasons through your assistant's existing claude / codex CLI sessions — there are no API keys and no direct cloud calls from insrc itself.

What the plugin does

  • One integration, four IDEs. A single artifact activates identically in IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm — it depends only on the shared platform module, so there is nothing IDE-specific to install or configure per product.
  • Wires your AI host automatically. On project open it detects your agentic assistant (JetBrains AI Assistant or Junie) and registers the insrc MCP server into that host's own configuration, plus the tracked-workflow steering into its rules file — so the assistant immediately knows to ground its answers and route features through insrc.
  • One-click project enablement. An "Enable insrc for this project" prompt registers the open project with the insrc daemon; every capability call is scoped to that project's own path, so a multi-project window keeps each repo's knowledge separate.
  • Manages the backing daemon for you. It ensures the daemon is present and up to date, and provisions a private, pinned Node runtime when the system one is missing or unsuitable — first-time setup is a single explicit consent, and later updates are silent and automatic.
  • Grounded analyze + tracked workflow, in your assistant. Once wired, your existing IDE assistant explores the code through the citation-grounded graph and can drive the full tracked design → review → plan → build workflow without leaving the IDE.
  • Clean and reversible. Every write into a host config or rules file is marker-delimited and preserves your own surrounding content. Uninstalling the plugin removes exactly those blocks and nothing else; a mere disable leaves them intact so re-enabling is instant.

How it works

The plugin holds no model logic of its own. It is a configuration orchestrator: it detects the host, writes the MCP + steering registration, registers the project with the daemon, and keeps the daemon healthy. All reasoning happens in your assistant, grounded by the daemon — the plugin simply makes the connection and stays out of the way.

Privacy

The plugin opens no cloud path and stores no credentials. The graph and vectors live on your disk; embeddings are computed locally; and all LLM access goes through your assistant's existing CLI/OAuth sessions. Nothing about your code leaves your machine because of this plugin.

Requirements

  • A JetBrains AI host (AI Assistant or Junie) — without one the plugin stays dormant and re-checks on later project opens, so it is safe to install ahead of time.
  • Node (used by the daemon); the plugin provisions a private runtime automatically if the system Node is missing or unsuitable.
  • The insrc daemon, which the plugin installs and keeps current on first use, with your consent.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.2

  • Expanded the Marketplace listing with a fuller description of what insrc is (local-first code-knowledge daemon: grounded analyze + tracked workflow) and how the plugin wires it into your IDE assistant. No functional changes.

0.1.1

  • Compatibility: removed the upper IDE-build bound — the plugin now loads on current and future IDE releases (2024.2 and later), since it depends only on the stable platform module.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Single-artifact activation across IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, and WebStorm.
  • AI-host detection (AI Assistant / Junie) with automatic MCP-server and tracked-workflow steering registration.
  • One-click project registration against the insrc daemon.
  • Daemon lifecycle management: presence/staleness check, consented first-time setup, tiered Node runtime.
  • Clean, reversible uninstall of all host-file writes.
